full_judgment: From a close reading of section 85 of the Evidence Act it appears that the said section only raises a presumption as to execution and authentication of a power-of-attorney executed and authenticated by the executants and the authority described in the section itself. Nowhere from the language of section 85 of the Evidence Act it could be read that a power-of-attorney executed by a person resident in Bangladesh like the present defendant No.1 and duly registered by a Sub-Registrar is not a legally valid document. In this case, it was not the case of the plaintiff that the defendant No. 1 did not execute the power-of-attorney and the same was not duly registered. Although registration of a power-of-attorney is not compulsory the power-of-attorney having been duly registered, under the provision of Registration Act and there being no challenge as to its genuineness of its execution by the petitioner I do not find any force in the contention of the learned Advocate for the opposite-party that the power-of-attorney cannot be accepted as a valid document. In my opinion although the power-of-attorney was not authenticated by a notary public as required under section 85 of the Evidence Act the same being executed by the petitioner and duly registered under the provisions of Registration Act is a valid document. In that view of the matter the written statement filed by the attorney of the defendant the petitioner on the strength of the said power-of-attorney was duly presented. Section 85 only raised a presumption regarding execution and authentication of power-of-attorney which is executed and authenticated outside the territory of Bangladesh but it does not say that a duly executed and registered power-of-attorney in Bangladesh unacceptable and invalid document for the reason of non-authentication. The learned advocate for the opposite-party also could not show from the record that the learned Additional District Judge expunged the written statement on any other ground or under Order II, rule 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
